articles.title: EvoRIC: Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuned LLM-empowered RAN Intelligent Control Toward Autonomous O-RAN
articles.selectionReason: Open full-text paper; topic ai; quality signal passed; application scenario is clear.

paperCard.problem: 给无线接入网（RAN）做智能控制时，传统机器学习换一个网络布局或环境就不太灵了；而直接用通用大语言模型（LLM）又太费算力，而且不懂通信领域的专业规则。
paperCard.method: 提出一个叫EvoRIC的分层架构，把控制分成两层：非实时RIC负责全局模型更新，近实时RIC负责本地执行，并让LLM在动态场景下获得通信领域的决策能力。
paperCard.difference: 和传统机器学习比，它靠LLM提升跨网络拓扑的泛化能力；和直接使用通用LLM比，它通过分层机制把大模型的计算压力分散，并注入领域知识。
paperCard.innovation: 把强化学习微调过的LLM嵌入到O-RAN的RIC架构里，让模型能随网络变化持续演进，既做全局更新又做本地执行。
paperCard.implementation: 在高层用非实时RIC做全局的模型训练和更新，在低层用近实时RIC做快速本地推理和决策；中间通过强化学习对LLM做领域微调，使其能适应不同网络状态。关键组件包括O-RAN标准中的RIC控制器、LLM和强化学习训练流程。
paperCard.applications: 适用于O-RAN环境下的无线资源管理、网络切片动态优化、移动性管理、流量预测与自动运维等需要智能决策的场景。
technicalTerms: O-RAN：开放无线接入网，把传统基站设备拆成可编程、可智能控制的模块。
RIC：无线接入网智能控制器，分为非实时和近实时两种。
LLM：大语言模型，能理解复杂指令的AI模型。
RL：强化学习，让AI通过试错和环境反馈来学习策略。

articles.highlight: 传统机器学习算法在不同网络拓扑下泛化能力有限，而通用大语言模型计算开销大且缺乏领域特定知识。
articles.summary: 这篇论文提出EvoRIC框架，通过分层架构将强化学习微调的大语言模型融入O-RAN的无线接入网智能控制中，以解决传统AI泛化差和通用大模型成本高的问题。它兼顾全局模型更新与本地执行，让网络控制能持续演进，值得关注。
articles.failureAnalysis: 摘要只给出框架设计，没有提供实验数据或性能验证，实际效果和计算开销是否真的可控仍属未知。
articles.sourceExcerpt: 1 EvoRIC: Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuned LLM-empowered RAN Intelligent Control Toward Autonomous O-RAN Lingyan Bao, Graduate Student Member , IEEE , Jemin Lee, Senior Member , IEEE, and Tony Q.S. Quek, Fellow, IEEE Abstract—Despite recent advances in applying artiﬁcial intel- ligence (AI) techniques to radio access network (RAN), crit ical challenges remain: traditional machine learning (ML) algo rithms suffer from limited generalization across varying network topolo- gies, whereas general-purpose large language models (LLMs ) face high computational demands and lack domain-speciﬁc knowledge. To address these gaps, this article introduces t he evolving RAN intelligent controller (RIC) (EvoRIC) framew ork, a hierarchical architecture that enables continuous evolu tion by leveraging a non-real-time RIC (non-RT RIC) for global model updates and a near-real-time RIC (near-RT RIC) for loc al execution, dynamically empowering LLMs with domain-speci ﬁc decision-making capabilities.

zh.title: EvoRIC：强化学习微调的大语言模型赋能的自主O-RAN智能控制框架
zh.highlight: 传统机器学习算法在不同网络拓扑下泛化能力有限，而通用大语言模型计算开销大且缺乏领域特定知识。
zh.summary: 这篇论文提出EvoRIC框架，通过分层架构将强化学习微调的大语言模型融入O-RAN的无线接入网智能控制中，以解决传统AI泛化差和通用大模型成本高的问题。它兼顾全局模型更新与本地执行，让网络控制能持续演进，值得关注。
zh.failureAnalysis: 摘要只给出框架设计，没有提供实验数据或性能验证，实际效果和计算开销是否真的可控仍属未知。

paperCard.problem: 给无线接入网（RAN）做智能控制时，传统机器学习换一个网络布局或环境就不太灵了；而直接用通用大语言模型（LLM）又太费算力，而且不懂通信领域的专业规则。
paperCard.method: 提出一个叫EvoRIC的分层架构，把控制分成两层：非实时RIC负责全局模型更新，近实时RIC负责本地执行，并让LLM在动态场景下获得通信领域的决策能力。
paperCard.difference: 和传统机器学习比，它靠LLM提升跨网络拓扑的泛化能力；和直接使用通用LLM比，它通过分层机制把大模型的计算压力分散，并注入领域知识。
paperCard.innovation: 把强化学习微调过的LLM嵌入到O-RAN的RIC架构里，让模型能随网络变化持续演进，既做全局更新又做本地执行。
paperCard.implementation: 在高层用非实时RIC做全局的模型训练和更新，在低层用近实时RIC做快速本地推理和决策；中间通过强化学习对LLM做领域微调，使其能适应不同网络状态。关键组件包括O-RAN标准中的RIC控制器、LLM和强化学习训练流程。
paperCard.applications: 适用于O-RAN环境下的无线资源管理、网络切片动态优化、移动性管理、流量预测与自动运维等需要智能决策的场景。
technicalTerms: O-RAN：开放无线接入网，把传统基站设备拆成可编程、可智能控制的模块。
RIC：无线接入网智能控制器，分为非实时和近实时两种。
LLM：大语言模型，能理解复杂指令的AI模型。
RL：强化学习，让AI通过试错和环境反馈来学习策略。

en.highlight: Traditional machine learning algorithms suffer from limited generalization across varying network topologies, whereas general-purpose LLMs face high computational demands and lack domain-specific knowledge.
en.summary: This paper proposes the EvoRIC framework, a hierarchical architecture that embeds reinforcement learning fine-tuned large language models into O-RAN intelligent control, addressing poor generalization of traditional AI and high cost of generic LLMs. It is worth reading because it balances global model updates and local execution for evolving network control.
en.failureAnalysis: The abstract only presents the framework design, with no experimental data or performance verification; actual effectiveness and computational cost remain unknown.
en.title: EvoRIC: Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuned LLM-empowered RAN Intelligent Control Toward Autonomous O-RAN

paperCard.problem: When applying AI to radio access network (RAN) control, traditional machine learning generalizes poorly across different network topologies, while directly using general-purpose large language models is computationally expensive and lacks communication domain knowledge.
paperCard.method: It proposes the EvoRIC framework, a hierarchical architecture that leverages a non-real-time RIC for global model updates and a near-real-time RIC for local execution, dynamically granting domain-specific decision-making capabilities to LLMs.
paperCard.difference: Compared with traditional machine learning, it uses LLMs to improve cross-topology generalization; compared with generic LLMs, it distributes computational load through hierarchy and injects domain knowledge.
paperCard.innovation: The innovation is embedding RL-fine-tuned LLMs into the O-RAN RIC architecture, enabling continuous model evolution while coordinating global and local control.
paperCard.implementation: A non-real-time RIC performs global model training and updates, while a near-real-time RIC handles fast local inference and decision-making; an RL loop fine-tunes the LLM to adapt to changing network conditions. Key components include O-RAN RIC, LLM, and RL training pipeline.
paperCard.applications: It can be applied to radio resource management, network slicing, mobility management, traffic prediction, and autonomous network operations in O-RAN.
technicalTerms: O-RAN: Open radio access network that decomposes traditional base stations into programmable, intelligently controlled modules.
RIC: RAN Intelligent Controller, with non-real-time and near-real-time variants.
LLM: Large language model, an AI model capable of understanding complex instructions.
RL: Reinforcement learning, letting AI learn strategies through trial and error with environment feedback.

articles.title: Physics-Grounded Materials Artificial Intelligence for Reliable Materials Discovery
articles.selectionReason: Open full-text paper; topic ai; quality signal passed; application scenario is clear.

paperCard.problem: 现有材料AI主要靠数据关联做预测，遇到没见过的新成分、新结构或新工况时经常猜不准，还会给出不稳定、做不出来甚至违反物理常识的材料。它要解决的问题就是让AI别只学数据表面，真正懂材料背后的物理规律。
paperCard.method: 提出“物理grounded材料AI”框架，把已知物理法则像搭积木一样融进AI的各个环节。具体分五层：物理当先验知识（先给模型科学常识）、物理当描述符（把复杂过程变成有用特征）、物理当约束（不许模型违反基本定律）、物理当验证器（用计算和实验检查AI结果）、物理当基础设施（建好可靠数据库）。
paperCard.difference: 以前的AI基本是黑箱，输入数据输出预测，不管物理对不对；这个框架强调物理不是辅助，而是贯穿数据表示、模型推理、验证和知识管理的主线，让AI从“只会匹配数据”升级为“能按物理机制推理”。
paperCard.innovation: 创新点是把分散的“物理+AI”做法统一成一个五层框架，并放在闭环工作流里：AI预测→物理/实验验证→结果再喂回模型，形成持续更新。还提出了从物理感知、物理推理到物理自主的发展路线图，目标是把AI变成能独立做科学发现的系统。
paperCard.implementation: 先用物理定律和数据库准备数据，再用机器学习、大语言模型和多智能体系统做性质预测和候选筛选；之后用密度泛函理论（DFT）等理论计算和实验表征验证预测；最后把验证结果反馈回数据库和模型，不断循环优化。文中用催化、固态电解质、储氢材料三个例子说明具体怎么嵌入物理知识。
paperCard.applications: 适用于需要高度可靠性的材料发现任务，比如催化材料筛选、固态电池固态电解质开发、储氢材料设计；也可推广到自动化实验和“AI科学家”式的自主科研系统，让AI在物理可行的空间里做机制引导的发现。
technicalTerms: 物理grounded：让AI根据物理规律而不是纯统计来学习，因此更可靠
先验知识：人类已有的科学结论，作为AI的初始常识，减少瞎猜
描述符：把材料的物理化学性质变成AI能处理的数字特征
约束：限制AI输出不许违反能量守恒、稳定性等基本定律
验证器：用理论计算或实验确认AI结果是否真实有效
闭环工作流：AI预测→验证→把结果反馈回去再学习，形成持续改进的循环
密度泛函理论：一种量子力学计算方法，常用来精确计算材料性质
大语言模型：像ChatGPT那样的模型，这里用来帮助读论文、自动推理

articles.highlight: 仅仅依赖数据拟合不足以支撑下一代材料智能，必须将物理定律嵌入模型构建、推理与验证全流程。
articles.summary: 本文提出“物理 grounded 材料 AI”框架，主张把热力学、动力学、电子结构等物理知识以先验、描述符、约束、验证器和基础设施五种角色融入AI，解决纯数据驱动方法可解释性差、外推能力弱、不符合物理规律的问题。文章以催化、固态电解质和储氢材料为例，给出了从物理感知AI到物理推理AI再到物理自主AI的路线图。
articles.failureAnalysis: 文章指出许多AI预测的无机材料缺乏真正新颖性、实验可信度和实用价值，且材料数据稀疏、异质、跨源偏差严重，即使嵌入物理知识，小样本与数据碎片化仍可能限制模型可靠性。
articles.sourceExcerpt: 1 Perspective Physics-Grounded Materials Artificial Intelligence for Reliable Materials Discovery Yuhang Wang, Qian Wang, Seong-Hoon Jang, and Hao Li* Advanced Institute for Materials Research (WPI-AIMR), Tohoku University, Sendai, 980-8577, Japan * Corresponding Authors: Email: li.hao.b8@tohoku.ac.jp (H. L.) 2 Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming materials discovery, yet conventional data -driven approaches often suffer from limited interpretability, poor extrapolation, and inconsistency with physical laws. Since materials behavior is fundamentally governed by thermodynamics, kinetics, electronic structure, transport processes, and operating environments, the next generation of materials intelligence must move beyond correlation-based prediction toward physics-grounded reasoning.

en.highlight: Relying on data alone is insufficient to support the next stage of materials intelligence; physical laws must be embedded throughout model construction, reasoning, and validation.
en.summary: This Perspective proposes a Physics-Grounded Materials AI (PhysMat AI) framework that integrates thermodynamic, kinetic, electronic-structure, and transport knowledge into AI through five roles: prior, descriptor, constraint, verifier, and infrastructure. Using catalysis, solid-state electrolytes, and hydrogen-storage materials as examples, it outlines a roadmap from physics-aware to physics-reasoning and ultimately physics-autonomous AI.
en.failureAnalysis: The paper notes that many AI-predicted inorganic compounds lack genuine novelty, experimental credibility, and practical utility, and that materials data remain sparse, heterogeneous, and fragmented—issues that can still limit reliability even when physics is embedded.
en.title: Physics-Grounded Materials Artificial Intelligence for Reliable Materials Discovery

paperCard.problem: Current materials AI mostly relies on statistical correlations, so it fails to extrapolate reliably to new compositions, structures, or operating conditions and can propose materials that are unstable, inaccessible, or violate basic physical laws.
paperCard.method: A unified framework that inserts physical knowledge into AI through five complementary roles: physics as prior knowledge, descriptor, constraint, verifier, and infrastructure, forming a closed-loop workflow from data to prediction to validation and feedback.
paperCard.difference: Unlike conventional black-box models that only fit data, this framework makes physics the central organizing principle across representation, reasoning, validation, and knowledge management, turning AI into a mechanism-guided discovery system.
paperCard.innovation: The innovation is the systematic five-layer architecture plus a closed-loop workflow, and the roadmap from physics-aware to physics-reasoning to physics-autonomous AI for autonomous scientific research.
paperCard.implementation: Start with physical laws and curated databases, use machine learning, large language models, and multi-agent systems to predict and screen candidates, then validate with DFT calculations and experiments, and feed validated data back into the model loop. Catalysis, SSE, and hydrogen-storage examples illustrate the concrete integration.
paperCard.applications: Reliable materials discovery in catalysis, solid-state batteries (solid-state electrolytes), hydrogen storage, and broader autonomous scientific research where physical feasibility and experimental verifiability matter.
technicalTerms: physics-grounded: making AI learn according to physical laws rather than pure statistics, improving reliability
prior knowledge: established scientific facts given to AI as initial context to reduce arbitrary guesses
descriptor: a numerical feature that encodes physical or chemical properties into a form AI can process
constraint: a restriction preventing AI outputs from violating conservation laws or stability principles
verifier: a theoretical or experimental check that confirms whether an AI prediction is actually valid
closed-loop workflow: a cycle of AI prediction, validation, and feedback into the model for continuous improvement
density functional theory: a quantum-mechanical method used to compute material properties accurately
large language model: a model like ChatGPT used here to assist literature reading and automatic reasoning
